case: rendered outcome: ground, card and readable ink hold in both themes
traceability: REGRESSION-RISK: auth-page rendered light/dark page ground, card surface and ink-on-card WCAG AA contrast — design/system/MASTER.md §Dark Mode Tokens > Implementation Rules > "9. Standalone auth pages (no tokens.css)", no feature-spec FR
reason: G3 SURVIVOR, WIDENED: the 4 cases the issue keeps (one per auth page). Each now asserts, in both themes, the computed body ground, the computed .card background (light rgb(255,255,255) / dark rgb(22,22,31)), the computed h1.card-title colour (light rgb(30,27,75) / dark rgb(226,232,240)), a >= 4.5 contrast ratio for that ink-on-card pair, and that neither .card-header nor the title itself paints a background, so the pair really is what the user sees. Proven by mutation: four quadrants (dark ink 1.12:1, light ink 1.23:1, light card value pin, dark card 1.23:1) plus three probes independent reviews found and these guards now close (a light-only .card-header background, a background on the title itself, and a translucent card that used to be scored as opaque black). NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR THE DELETED PINS, IT CHANGES AXIS: these assertions read rendered colour, so they are stronger where a page consumes the wrong token or overrides it in one theme, and weaker on three source-text clauses they cannot see. (1) Whether the tokens are declared and re-mapped at all: hardcoding .card background in both themes with no --color-card declaration passes every case, where the deleted pins failed. (2) Whether the local names are canonical: renaming --color-card to --auth-card-bg, still declared and re-mapped in both themes, also passes (verified) -- a different axis from (1). (3) The deprecated-name hygiene rule, whose names no page consumes, so no rendered assertion can see a re-declaration. All three belong in the node gate, which already reads these page shells as source. Also uncovered: --color-primary-soft-bg, consumed only in :hover rules. AND ONE LIVE DEFECT, NOT JUST A GAP: --color-ink-muted is still #94A3B8 on all four pages, which is 2.564:1 for .card-subtitle 15px normal text on the white card -- a WCAG AA failure today, the same value issue #973 raised to #64748B in tokens.css, a fix these pages never received. These rows assert the title pair only; they do not certify the card as AA-clean. On the threshold: .card-title is 22px/700, i.e. WCAG large text whose AA minimum is 3:1, and MASTER colours measure 15.99:1 / 14.58:1 -- 3.55x and 3.24x of the asserted floor -- so the ratio catches gross failures only. Residual gaps tracked in issue #1067; the #94A3B8 defect in #1069.
